titulo: 8 New Year Promises Ranked by Cella: Which Ones Last
caption: YouTube only (a medio in 16:9, no Short and no Reel). What goes out is the YouTube title and the description.
descripcion:
On the thirty-first, people promise to become somebody else by Friday. In Cella's notes, most of those promises are gone by the second week of January. Cella ranks eight promise archetypes, all about behavior, by how long each one lasts.

Chapters
0:00 The date and the rules
0:38 #8 The New Person
1:06 #7 Never Late Again
1:36 #6 Reply to Everything
2:05 #5 Stop Complaining
2:36 #4 Call a Friend
3:04 #3 Say No on Time
3:38 #2 Finish One Thing
4:10 #1 The Two-Minute Step
4:46 #0 This ranking, and what lasts

The eight are archetypes, not people and not brands, and every one was made sincerely. The scores (lasts, out of ten) and the whole ranking are Cella's opinion and nothing in it is a study. The one thing the long-lasting ones share, by her reading: they are small, specific, and tied to a paper or a person.

Voice: synthetic. Music and sounds made with code by NAOS.
Choose friction.

At night, Cella, a small amber doorway-shaped figure with two white eyes, sits on a bench next to a lamp and ranks eight New Year promise archetypes by how long each one lasts, on a sheet on the left with what the promise says, when it breaks and a lasts score out of ten. Number 8, the New Person, 1 of 10. Number 7, Never Late Again, 2. Number 6, Reply to Everything, 3. Number 5, Stop Complaining, 4. Number 4, Call a Friend Every Week, 6. Number 3, Say No on Time, 7. Number 2, Finish One Thing, 8. Number 1, the Two-Minute Step, 9 of 10. A bonus entry, number 0, is the ranking itself. The ones that last are small, specific and tied to a paper or a person; Cella's own promise this year is to finish one thing before starting another. Final cards: For whoever is writing a promise tonight; Choose friction.
